channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: Mobile Operators Fined for Exceeding Signal Levels in Kostanay Region Prisons
item.description: Three major mobile operators in Kazakhstan have been fined for exceeding permissible signal levels within correctional facilities in the Kostanay region. The regional prosecutor's office, in conjunction with radio frequency services, found violations by Beeline, Kcell, and ALTEL/Tele2. The operators failed to comply with regulations requiring signal optimization within prison premises.

item.title: Central Asian Turkic States Propose Joint Medical University
item.description: Health ministers from the Organization of Turkic States met in Bishkek, where Kazakhstan proposed establishing a joint medical university. This initiative aims to unite leading medical institutions, jointly train doctors, facilitate specialist exchange, and advance medical science. The proposal also includes creating a coordination council for medical education within the Turkic States Organization.

item.title: Oil Tanker Struck by Unidentified Projectile Off Oman Coast, No Injuries Reported
item.description: An oil tanker was hit by an unidentified projectile approximately four nautical miles east of Oman, according to the UK Maritime Trade Operations. The tanker's captain reported the incident, but no crew members were injured and no environmental damage was sustained. The responsible party remains unclear, though tensions between Iran and the US are high.

item.title: Kazakhstan Proposes Establishing a Networked Medical University for Turkic States
item.description: Kazakhstan's Ministry of Health has proposed creating a networked university by uniting leading medical institutions of Turkic states. This initiative aims to enable joint development of educational programs, including public health and bioinformatics, and facilitate international internships for young scientists and doctors.

item.title: Belgian Interior Minister: Criminal Afghan Migrants Should Be Deported
item.description: Belgium's Interior Minister stated that approximately 60 Afghan nationals with illegal residency, including convicted murderers and rapists, should be deported after serving their sentences. She emphasized that allowing them to remain would be inhumane and urged coalition partners to prioritize returns.

item.title: Zarafshan Glacier in Tajikistan Shrank by 11.7% Over 32 Years
item.description: The Zarafshan glacier basin in Tajikistan has lost 17.5 sq km, or 11.7%, of its ice area between 1992 and 2024, while average temperatures rose by 1 degree Celsius. Researchers attribute this degradation to rising temperatures, changing precipitation, and pollution, warning of further 15-20% shrinkage in 30-40 years.

item.title: Western countries plan to move embassies from Kyiv amid emergency concerns
item.description: Western nations are reportedly planning to relocate their embassies from Kyiv. According to The Guardian, contingency plans are being developed to move diplomatic missions to Lviv or eastern Poland in case of an emergency in Kyiv.

item.title: Belgian Minister Proposes Deportation of Convicted Afghan Nationals After Sentence Completion
item.description: Belgium's Minister for Asylum and Migration, Anneleen Van Bossuyt, stated that Afghan nationals convicted of crimes and residing illegally in Belgium should be deported to Afghanistan after serving their prison sentences. She emphasized that these discussions do not imply support for the Islamic Emirate of Afghanistan and are aimed at addressing security concerns, including the safety of women and girls.

item.title: Elderly Almaty Pensioner Kidnapped for Property by Three Individuals
item.description: Three individuals in Almaty kidnapped an 81-year-old single pensioner from his home, holding him captive for several days. They allegedly tortured the elderly man and demanded he sign over his sole property to them. The victim was found in a private house in a settlement near Almaty. Three suspects have been charged with kidnapping, illegal detention, and extortion.

item.title: Personal Data of Over 500 Teachers Illegally Published Online in Kazakhstan
item.description: Personal data of 529 teachers from seven educational institutions in Kazakhstan's Kyzylorda region were illegally published on the state procurement portal. Prosecutors intervened to remove the data and disciplined the responsible officials. This incident follows previous reports of data leaks and international networks selling personal information.

item.title: Kazakhstan's National Bank Conducts Cyber Exercises with Foreign Central Banks
item.description: The National Bank of Kazakhstan participated in international cyber exercises named 'Cyber Alem 2026' with central banks from other countries. The drills focused on responding to potential cyberattacks and global incidents to maintain high cyber resilience. This initiative aims to foster international cooperation in cybersecurity.

item.title: Kazakhstan Fines Three Mobile Operators for Strong Signal in Correctional Facilities
item.description: Three major Kazakh mobile operators, Beeline, Kcell, and Tele2/Altel, have been fined for exceeding permissible mobile signal levels within three correctional facilities in the Kostanay region. The fines were issued after a joint inspection by the prosecutor's office and the State Radio Frequency Service revealed non-compliance with regulations requiring signal reduction in such institutions. Previously, crimes committed using mobile phones were detected in these facilities.

item.title: Uzbek Banks Face Restrictions Up to Six Months for Deceptive Credit Offers
item.description: Uzbekistan's Central Bank has introduced new regulations allowing for restrictions of up to six months on banks offering deceptive credit products. Banks must now include warnings in their advertisements about potential financial risks for consumers failing to meet credit obligations. These warnings must occupy a significant portion of the advertisement space. The new rules come into effect one month after official publication.

item.title: Tajikistan and Mongolia Units Thwart Counterattack During CSTO Center-2026 Drills
item.description: Units from Tajikistan and Mongolia successfully prevented a simulated enemy counterattack during the Center-2026 strategic command and staff exercises at the Chebarkul training ground. Mobile armored groups were deployed to block the advance of reserve units. The exercise involved over 6,000 personnel, including contingents from Russia and other CSTO member states.

item.title: Kazakhstan Extradites Suspect in Major Fraud Case After Five Years
item.description: Kazakhstan's National Security Committee (KNB) has extradited a citizen suspected of large-scale fraud who had been evading justice abroad for five years. The individual was apprehended and returned to Astana on October 2, 2021, and is now in a pre-trial detention center.

item.title: Lithuanian Border Guards Detain 35 Afghan and Iraqi Migrants Crossing from Belarus
item.description: Lithuanian border guards apprehended 35 Afghan and Iraqi migrants near Katras village after they crossed from Belarus. A large-scale operation involving a helicopter, special forces, and dogs located the group. Twenty-nine were denied entry and returned to Belarus.

item.title: Kazakhstan Extradites Citizen Sought Internationally for Fraud
item.description: A citizen of Kazakhstan, who was internationally wanted for large-scale fraud, has been extradited back to the country. The National Security Committee (KNB) reported the operation, which involved cooperation with Interpol and the General Prosecutor's Office. The suspect had been evading justice since 2021 and is now in pre-trial detention.

item.title: Former Hungarian PM Viktor Orbán May Face Criminal Charges Over Ukrainian Arrests
item.description: Former Hungarian Prime Minister Viktor Orbán may face criminal charges for allegedly ordering the illegal detention of Ukrainian bank employees. The head of Hungary's counter-terrorism police involved in the operation has reportedly been dismissed. The details of the case are still emerging.

item.title: Suspect in Major Fraud Case Extradited to Kazakhstan
item.description: A Kazakhstani citizen, wanted internationally for large-scale fraud, has been extradited to Kazakhstan. The National Security Committee (KNB) reported the operation, conducted on October 2, involved cooperation with Interpol and the Prosecutor General's Office. The suspect had been evading justice since 2021 and is now in pre-trial detention.

item.title: Kazakhstan MFA responds to appeals from citizens recruited for conflict
item.description: Kazakhstan's Ministry of Foreign Affairs has established a hotline to receive appeals from relatives of Kazakh citizens involved in conflict zones. The ministry is in consultations with Russia regarding joint measures to return citizens and is monitoring the situation closely.

item.title: Kazakhstan, Uzbekistan, UAE sign MoU for CASA railway project via Afghanistan
item.description: Kazakhstan, Uzbekistan, and the United Arab Emirates have signed a Memorandum of Understanding to cooperate on the Kazakhstan-Uzbekistan-Afghanistan-Pakistan (CASA) railway project. This initiative aims to establish a new rail route connecting Central and South Asia, providing access to Pakistan's ports.

item.title: Tokayev Praises Astana AI Film Festival as Unique, Unprecedented Project
item.description: Kazakh President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev described the Astana AI Film Festival as a unique, unparalleled project, highlighting the rapid growth of creative industries in Kazakhstan. He emphasized the festival showcases innovative citizens and reflects the era of knowledge, science, and AI's transformative impact on the global economy. Tokayev also stressed the importance of responsible AI use amid growing concerns about its uncontrolled development.

item.title: Yemeni Army Claims Over 1,500 Houthi Fighters Killed or Wounded in 24 Hours
item.description: The Yemeni army reported that 1,540 Houthi fighters were killed or wounded in the past 24 hours following 474 airstrikes and operations. A spokesperson stated most casualties occurred in Taiz, with significant destruction of Houthi military equipment. The operations spanned various regions, while Houthis accused Saudi Arabia of targeting civilian areas.

item.title: Pediatric Surgeon Detained in Aktau Following Child's Death
item.description: A pediatric surgeon at the regional children's hospital in Aktau has been detained on suspicion of professional misconduct. Pre-trial investigation is underway following the death of a minor patient. Police investigations revealed errors in medical care, leading to complications. The child was airlifted to Almaty but later died. The surgeon is in temporary detention.

item.title: Flydubai Co-Pilot Admits Planning to Crash Plane in Israel
item.description: The co-pilot of a Flydubai flight, who previously attacked the captain, has reportedly confessed to investigators that he intended to crash the aircraft in Israel. The Omani national, identified as 29-year-old Hamam al-Hammami, is cooperating with authorities. He was previously found with extremist materials but allowed to continue flying.

item.title: Ukraine Asks Kazakhstan Not to Extradite Ukrainian Woman to Russia
item.description: Ukraine's embassy in Kazakhstan has requested authorities not to extradite Lyubov Rozhanskaya to Russia. She was detained in Astana after arriving from Istanbul. Ukrainian diplomats are seeking access to Rozhanskaya, who is in pre-trial detention, and are working with her lawyers to protect her rights. Russia seeks her extradition over alleged child abduction attempts.

item.title: Additional $300 Million Allocated for Rogun Hydropower Project
item.description: Parliament has approved an additional $300 million for the Rogun Hydropower Project. These funds are intended for the implementation of the second phase of the project. Further details are available.

item.title: Migrant Workers in Kazakhstan Earn Average Monthly Income of $984, Lacks Pension Contributions
item.description: A survey by the International Organization for Migration found that migrant workers in Kazakhstan earn an average of $984 per month. Nearly half of respondents reported no pension contributions. The study surveyed 2,604 foreign workers across 11 regions and major cities, with most coming from Uzbekistan, Russia, and Tajikistan.

item.title: UN Women: 60% of Afghans at Risk of Food Insecurity, Women and Girls Disproportionately Affected
item.description: UN Women reports that 60% of individuals at risk of food insecurity in Afghanistan are women and girls. The agency estimates an additional 11.7 million women and girls in 28 countries may face food insecurity by the end of 2026. Around 95% of Afghan women are outside the labor market, with 80% of employed women in vulnerable jobs.

item.title: Former Head of Uzbekistan's State Security Service Under House Arrest
item.description: Abdusalom Azizov, former head of Uzbekistan's State Security Service (SSS), is reportedly under house arrest. Sources in law enforcement told Ozodlik (RFE/RL's Uzbek Service) that Azizov was dismissed in mid-August and arrested the same day. A Tashkent court later placed him under house arrest.

item.title: Uzbekistan's LPG Market Sees Sharp Changes After Price Cap Removal
item.description: Uzbekistan's liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) market experienced significant shifts in September following the removal of price restrictions on the stock exchange. A presidential decree mandated that domestically produced and imported LPG be sold exclusively through the exchange, effective September 15. This led to a sharp increase in the exchange price of propane, raising concerns about potential price hikes at gas stations.

item.title: Pakistan Generals Demand Action Against Terrorist Bases in Afghanistan
item.description: Senior Pakistani military commanders have called for action against alleged terrorist positions within Afghanistan. Following recent strikes, Pakistani generals deemed them successful counterterrorism operations and asserted the nation's right to self-defense. They blamed the Taliban leadership for providing a platform for terrorism, holding them responsible for consequences.

item.title: Kazakhstan to Require Open Display of Commissions for Taxi and Courier Services
item.description: New regulations in Kazakhstan may require internet platforms like Yandex, inDrive, and Glovo to openly display commission amounts deducted from each order. The Ministry of Labor proposes simplifying registration, allowing platforms to access state databases for driver information. Taxi drivers also seek consistent pension contributions.

item.title: Kazakhstan Opens First Central Asian AI University, Enters Guinness World Records
item.description: Kazakhstan has launched the Qazaq AI Research University in Astana, the first institution in Central Asia integrating artificial intelligence into all core processes from education to management. President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev inaugurated the university, which was established in under a year and currently enrolls 528 students.

item.title: Ukraine Asks Kazakhstan Not to Extradite Citizen Detained in Astana
item.description: Ukraine's embassy in Kazakhstan has requested that Astana not extradite Lyubov Rozhanskaya, a Ukrainian citizen detained while attempting to take her granddaughter. Ukrainian diplomats have visited Rozhanskaya and are in contact with her lawyers. Kazakhstan authorities detained Rozhanskaya, who faces charges in Russia for attempted child abduction.

item.title: Pakistan: Mecca Pact Members to Discuss Engaging Houthis After Attacks
item.description: Pakistan's foreign minister stated that Iran has suggested politically engaging Yemen's Houthis following recent attacks. The committee of the Mecca defense pact will discuss this proposal at an emergency meeting in Riyadh. Saudi Arabia, Turkey, and Pakistan, the pact's members, will determine the next steps. Iran has reportedly distanced itself from the Houthis.

item.title: Taliban Claim Repelling Attack by Opposition Forces in Kamdesh District
item.description: The Taliban claim to have repelled an attack by over 100 opposition fighters in Kamdesh district, Nuristan province. This marks the first time the Taliban admit such a large number of opposition fighters entering Afghanistan. The opposition group, Afghanistan Freedom Front, confirmed clashes and claimed casualties among Taliban forces. The Taliban accused Pakistan of supporting the attackers.

item.title: United Front Claims Taliban Policeman Killed in Kandahar Operation
item.description: The Afghanistan United Front claims responsibility for killing a Taliban member in Kandahar. The group stated on X that its forces killed the fighter during an operation in the Sarband area of Arghandab district on Friday. This claim follows recent reports of increased anti-Taliban activity across the country.

item.title: Xinjiang Kazakh Daughter Denied Citizenship in Kazakhstan Due to Unresolved Marriage Issues
item.description: A Kazakh girl from Xinjiang, Rayana, faces difficulties obtaining citizenship in Kazakhstan because her father, Abir Dalelkhan, cannot legally prove their parentage. His previous marriage in China was not officially dissolved, preventing his second marriage registration and subsequently complicating the documentation for his daughter born in China.

item.title: Second Ship Attacked in Strait of Hormuz Within 24 Hours
item.description: A second vessel has been targeted in the Strait of Hormuz within the past 24 hours. Details regarding the nature of the attack and any potential casualties or damage remain scarce. This incident follows a previous attack in the same strategic waterway, raising concerns about maritime security.
